ladder.d.theta: Angle between ladder and floor; dragging the top along the wall changes it too
ladder.d.d: Distance from the foot of the ladder to the person, along the ladder; dragging the person changes it too
ladder.d.m: Mass of the uniform ladder; its centre of mass is at the middle
ladder.d.M: Mass of the person on the ladder; 0 removes the person
ladder.d.mu: Coefficient of static friction between floor and ladder foot
ladder.d.crit: Show the ladder at the critical angle $\theta_c$ (dashed) and the critical position $d_c$
ladder.goal.cond: Two conditions for static equilibrium: net force $\sum\vec F = 0$ and net torque $\sum\vec\tau = 0$
ladder.goal.pivot: With the pivot at the foot, $N$ and $f$ exert no torque → the torque equation has a single unknown, $F_w$
ladder.goal.limit: Equilibrium holds only while the friction it needs, $f = F_w$, does not exceed the maximum static friction $\mu_s N$
ladder.obs.drag: Drag the person along the ladder; drag the top along the wall to change the angle
ladder.obs.climb: As the person climbs, the lever arm $d\cos\theta$ of $Mg$ grows → $F_w$ and the needed friction grow; $N$ stays the same
ladder.obs.angle: A smaller angle lengthens the weights' lever arms and shortens that of $F_w$, $L\sin\theta$ → more friction needed
ladder.obs.crit: Dashed ladder = critical angle $\theta_c$; bar across the ladder = critical position $d_c$ (climbing higher makes it slip)
ladder.obs.slip: Gauge past 100 %: the friction arrow stops at $\mu_s N$ and the missing part is dashed → no equilibrium, the foot slips away from the wall
ladder.obs.arms: Dimension lines below and to the left = lever arms about the foot: $(L/2)\cos\theta$, $d\cos\theta$, $L\sin\theta$
ladder.asm.wall: Frictionless wall → its force $F_w$ is horizontal. The floor exerts a normal force $N$ and static friction $f$
ladder.asm.body: Uniform ladder (length $L$ = 5 m, centre of mass at the middle); the person's weight $Mg$ acts on the ladder at the rung at $d$; $g$ = 9.8 m/s²
ladder.asm.slip: Past the limit there is no static equilibrium: the arrows show the forces equilibrium would need; the ladder actually starts to slip (its motion is not computed)
ladder.asm.scale: Arrow length ∝ force (400 N = 1 m; all arrows shrink when the longest would exceed 2.2 m)
